name: Chocolate Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Beat whites and yolks separately first, and then together; beat into this sugar, and then melted butter.
Sift flour into which you have stirred two teaspoons baking powder and a pinch of salt.
Beat it gradually into the eggs, etc., and then add enough milk to make a moderately stiff batter.
Bake in two layer cake tins in quick oven.
Melt chocolate in teacup boiling water on stove; add sugar enough to stiffen it into a thick paste; put this between layers while they are hot and ice top of cake.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat whites and yolks separately first, and then together; beat into this sugar, and then melted butter.
2. Sift flour into which you have stirred two teaspoons baking powder and a pinch of salt.
3. Beat it gradually into the eggs, etc., and then add enough milk to make a moderately stiff batter.
4. Bake in two layer cake tins in quick oven.
5. Melt chocolate in teacup boiling water on stove; add sugar enough to stiffen it into a thick paste; put this between layers while they are hot and ice top of cake.
